gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws every stroke at a single measured thickness, with no pressure variation. Noto Sans Vithkuqi handles the quieter job, keeping its throats open and its capitals close to the lowercase in height.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Megrim is all angles and hairline-free strokes, with a c as open as a bent paperclip. And Noto Sans Wancho is the heavy one, a hulking lowercase that would swamp the heading if the heading were made small.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks. Megrim is the sharper act, its horizontal bars as heavy as its stems, while the sans body keeps wide channels leading into each counter.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-square: Approachable and tall in the x-height, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square keeps its wide gaps crisp even at tiny sizes. Megrim sits above with horizontals as thick as its verticals.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Noto Traditional Nushu reads like a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, with bowls filling the line. Noto Traditional Nushu is friendly, yet Megrim's texture, like neatly bent pipe cleaner, gives the pair its edge.
gen-megrim-gf-numans: Megrim brings angular, futuristic strokes that all end at the same measured thickness, a skyward x-height line above everything. Numans answers with loose, widely tracked sans.
gen-megrim-gf-onest: Onest reads approachably, with short ascenders sitting above big bowls and a gentle monotone of line thickness. And Megrim's angular, bent-wire heading lets that plain sans body run on smoothly, with no ink pooling where curves turn in.
gen-megrim-gf-open-sans: Open Sans reads smoothly, with no clogged curves anywhere in its bulky lowercase. Open Sans keeps a long stretch of text moving, while Megrim's line width stays the same in curves and straights.
gen-megrim-gf-orienta: Orienta reads with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open, and little height difference between cases. And Megrim's stems and arcs move in lockstep, so a long plain sans passage under it would feel light and unhurried.
gen-megrim-gf-oxygen: Contemporary and angular, Megrim draws every stroke at one thickness. Oxygen follows with curves that never close back on themselves, and lowercase nearly matching the capitals, so a longer passage glides along.
